source.title: Timely sleep facilitates declarative memory consolidation in infants
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: This is the first experimental (not merely correlational) causal demonstration that offline consolidation benefit in human infants (6- and 12-month-olds) is TIME-SENSITIVE -- a nap within 4 hours of learning was necessary for retention at both 4h and 24h delays, and a single nap of at least 30 minutes was sufficient. This directly supports MECH-533's frequency-half of the joint claim (DEV-NEED-007): frequent, well-timed offline windows matter causally, not just correlationally, in infancy specifically -- and the requirement for TIMELY placement (not just occurrence) of an offline window is itself evidence that infant offline-processing capacity is a scarce, time-window-limited resource, consistent with a system whose offline competence is still developing rather than uniformly available.
failure_signatures: This paper demonstrates the FREQUENCY/TIMING half of MECH-533's joint claim (offline windows must be timely and sufficiently long) but does not itself measure offline-processing COMPETENCE separately -- it cannot by itself establish the CONDITIONAL/CROSSED relationship MECH-533 requires (that frequency benefit depends on competence level), only that frequency/timing matters at all in infancy.

The task is deferred imitation (a simple declarative/procedural hybrid memory task testing whether infants reproduce a modeled action sequence after a delay), a much simpler memory demand than REE's cross-episode replay-dependent reorganisation or generalisation -- the transfer from 'infants need a timely nap to retain a modeled action sequence' to REE's offline-competence architecture is substantial.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Infants aged 6 and 12 months who napped within 4 hours of learning a modeled action sequence (deferred imitation task) retained the learned sequence at both 4-hour and 24-hour delays; infants who did not nap within that window failed to retain it. A single nap of at least 30 minutes was sufficient to produce the retention benefit. This is presented as the first experimental causal demonstration of offline consolidation's time-sensitivity in year-one infants.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-533's joint/conditional claim states that offline frequency and offline COMPETENCE co-mature -- frequent early offline windows are needed because early traces are fragile, and DEV-NEED-007 (frequent offline integration during early development) already names the frequency half. Seehagen et al. provide a causal (not merely observational) demonstration that infant memory retention genuinely depends on offline-window TIMING and occurrence, strengthening the empirical basis for DEV-NEED-007's frequency claim specifically. This constrains WHEN offline processing must be triggered relative to experience -- directly relevant to any REE implementation of a developmental offline-window scheduler.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This paper evidences the frequency/timing-matters half of MECH-533's joint claim; it does not itself measure or manipulate offline-processing COMPETENCE as a separate variable, so it cannot alone establish the CROSSED (frequency benefit conditional on competence) relationship that is MECH-533's distinguishing claim over a pure frequency account. It should be read as one half of the joint claim's evidential basis, paired with the competence-maturation evidence in the companion Pochinok (2024) and Noguchi (2023) entries in this same directory.
mapping.source_context: Human infants aged 6 and 12 months; deferred imitation task (modeled action sequence on novel objects); nap timing (within vs. after a 4-hour window) as the natural/quasi-experimental manipulation; retention tested at 4-hour and 24-hour delays.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality: the first genuinely causal (not just correlational) demonstration of offline consolidation time-sensitivity in year-one human infants, in a top general-science venue. Mapping fidelity moderate: strongly grounds MECH-533's frequency/timing half (DEV-NEED-007) but does not itself test the competence half or the crossed relationship, which is why it is banked alongside the competence-focused Pochinok and Noguchi entries in this same directory.
